sentences.text: CM APPL. 19327/2022 (Seeking condonation of delay in filing the review petition)

1. The instant application has been filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 on behalf of the applicants/claimants/respondents seeking condonation of delay of 882 days in filing the accompanying review petition against the order/judgment dated 21st September, 2017 passed by the Predecessor Bench of this Court.
2. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the applicant submitted that the insurance company filed the appeal against the judgment and order dated 23rd July, 2010 passed by the learned Tribunal.
It is submitted that the appellant had filed the captioned appeal challenging the said order of the This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 23/08/2024 at 23:45:22 learned Tribunal, however, the Predecessor Bench of this Court had disposed of the same by modifying the award, in the absence of counsel for applicants/respondents.
3. It is further submitted that the counsel who was engaged by the claimants/applicants herein mislead them regarding the status of appeal and reduction in the compensation.

sentences.text:
It is submitted that the said counsel never informed the applicants regarding the decision/judgment passed by the Predecessor Bench of this Court, and when the claimants did not receive any information by the counsel engaged on earlier occasion regarding the captioned appeal,
they checked the status of the appeal and found that the appeal was already decided on 21st September, 2017 wherein the award was modified.
5.

It is submitted that as soon as the applicants/claimants/respondents came to the knowledge of the aforesaid judgment of the Predecessor Bench of this Court, they approached their current counsel on 11th December, 2021, pursuant to which the certified copy of the entire record was applied in the Registry of this Court which was received on 5th April, 2022, and accordingly, the accompanying review petition was filed.
6.

It is submitted that the claimants could not filed the review petition within the prescribed limitation period due to the facts as stated above and that the delay caused in filing the accompanying review petition is bona fide and unintentional and therefore, the delay of 882 days in filing review petition may be condoned and the review petition may be heard on merits.
7. Per contra, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the non- applicant/appellant vehemently opposed the instant application for condoning the extraordinary delay of 882 days.
This is a digitally signed order.

It is submitted that in the application filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963, the applicant has not assigned any reason for condoning the extraordinary delay.

It is submitted that it is settled law that while adjudicating the extraordinary delay in filing the appeal/review petition,
every dates causing the delay shall be explained.
9. It is submitted that paragraphs 3 and 4 of the application are not disclosing any appropriate and cogent reasons for condoning the delay of 882 days in filing the accompanying review petition.
10. It is submitted that whatever grounds mentioned in the review petition are not the grounds for reviewing the order dated 21st September, 2017.

It is submitted that this Court has a limited scope in the review jurisdiction to review the orders and as such there are no grounds available to the applicant on merit to show that there are errors apparent on record.
11.

It is submitted that there is no force in the arguments that the applicant was not informed by the previous counsel as it is settled law that every client is equally responsible to pursue the matter with the counsel or in the Court.

Further, all the information regarding the status of the case is available on the website of this High Court and merely blaming the counsel for not informing the applicant is not appropriate ground for condoning the extraordinary delay.

Also, if any professional misconduct,
as alleged in the application, is done by any counsel, the applicant chose not to take any action or file New India Assurance Co Ltd vs Manju Devi & Ors on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26942200/
2 any complaint before the Bar Council.

sentences.text: 12. Therefore, the instant application is liable to be dismissed with cost being devoid of any merit.
13. Heard learned counsel appearing on behalf of the parties and perused the record.

The applicant has given the grounds for condonation of delay in paragraph nos. 3 and 4 of the instant application which are reproduced herein under:
"3. That the above final judgment and order dated 21.09.2017 was passed in the absence of the counsel for applicants/ claimants, through they engaged the same counsel engaged in trial court for above appeal, but the counsel kept them misleading regarding the status of appeal and the reduction in the compensation and when the earlier counsel could not provide any information, then the claimants approached the undersigning counsel on 11.12 2021, and when the status of case was checked it was found to be decided vide above judgment and order dated 21.09.2017, and then the claimants came to know about the fate of this appeal, they immediately collected their documents and instructed the undersigning counsel to get the order corrected in the month of January 2022, then the undersigning counsel applied for certified copy of entire record from this Hon'ble Court and received the same on 05.04.2022.
4.

That the claimants could not approach this Hon'ble Court within limitation period due to the fact that their counsel did not give them the true and actual information and status of the case, and the applicants/claimants are illiterate persons whereas two of the claimants were minor and old aged father and widow lady and sister of deceased, and the widow is working on daily basis in a factory, at the time of final disposal, furthermore the delay is caused due to Covid-19 pandemic situation throught country.

Hoever, the review application is filed within limitation period from the date when the certified copy of record with judgment and order dated 21.09.2017 is received, but there is delay of 882 days from the date of order."
15. In paragraph nos. 3 and 4, only three dates were mentioned for explaining the delay of 882 days.

sentences.text: In G. Ramegowda v. Spl. Land Acquisition Officer, (1988) 2 SCC 142, the Honble Supreme Court held that delays in preferring appeals are required to be condoned in the interest of justice where no gross negligence or deliberate inaction or lack of bona fide is imputable to the party seeking condonation of the delay.

entities.text: G. Ramegowda v. Spl. Land Acquisition Officer, (1988) 2 SCC 142
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. Insofar as the law is concerned, it is a well-settled principle that the determination of what constitutes sufficient cause cannot be governed by any inflexible rule but must be adjudicated by the Courts based on the peculiar facts and circumstances surrounding each individual case.
18. The applicants herein contend that due to the fault of the counsel to inform the appellant about the case, the review petition could not be filed within the prescribed time.

With regard to the same,
the Honble Division Bench of Madras High Court in M. Subramania Mudaliar v. K. Janardhanam,
1993 SCC OnLine Mad 204 observed that such contention is not a valid ground to seek condonation of delay.

sentences.text: 19. Applying the aforesaid discussion of law to the facts of the instant case, this Court is not satisfied that the applicants have diligently pursued the matter.
The applicants have not placed any material on record to show that at any point of time it had enquired from its earlier counsel with regard to the progress of the matter.
Further, the current counsel has also failed to provide two dates as to when he applied for the documents.
On the specific query of the Court, he has also failed to reply as to when the applicants approached the previous counsel, whether he was approached orally or was This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 23/08/2024 at 23:45:31 he approached by way of writing any email or letter.

20. As per one of the latest judgments of the Honble Supreme Court passed in Mool Chandra v.
Union of India, 2024 SCC OnLine SC 1878, it is held that if negligence can be attributed to the applicant, then necessarily the delay may not be condoned, however, if no fault can be ascribed to the applicant and cause shown is sufficient, then the delay may be condoned.

Union of India, 2024 SCC OnLine SC 1878
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 21. Therefore, this Court is of the considered view that it was the duty of the applicants to be aware and informed of the status of the case in which they are the parties as it is settled that the litigant is equally responsible to pursue the matter in the Court.

Whatever reasons given in the instant application in paragraph nos. 3 and 4 are certainly not cogent reasons for condoning the inordinate delay of 882 days and hence, this Court does not find any merit in the instant application due to absence of any sufficient cause.
In view of the same, the arguments advanced by the applicants are legally untenable on the face of it and do not fall within the ambit of sufficient cause.
22. Accordingly, the instant application stands dismissed.

Since the application for condonation of delay has already been dismissed by this Court being devoid of any merit, this Court does not find any reason to adjudicate the instant review petition on New India Assurance Co Ltd vs Manju Devi & Ors on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26942200/
4 merits.
However, after plain reading of the review petition and grounds made therein, this Court does not find any merit in the review petition for reviewing the order dated 21st September, 2017, as whatever grounds are taken before this Court prima facie seem to be grounds for appeal.
